<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Checking additional project files and code paths.

Several specific issues stand out. UDPReceiver.messageQueue appears unused outside its own class. DiscoverServerAsync is defined but never invoked. HarmonyEngineTests lacks an asmdef, so it compiles into Assembly-CSharp and RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod runs in the player. MIDIConnectionManager calls FindObjectOfType every frame. Need to verify whether UDPBeacon and UDPReceiver use DontDestroyOnLoad. Also reviewing DTO files, comment quality, and emoji usage.

A triple polling layer exists for MIDI status. DirectMidiReceiver polls JNI every millisecond. MIDIStatusReceiver polls every half second. MIDIConnectionManager.RefreshStateFromReceiver runs every frame. This redundancy is a major performance concern.

MidiStatusWidgetController.RefreshView runs every 0.1 seconds. QuestXRInteractionController.Diagnostics.cs is actively used at runtime. LogHands, LogHandsWarning, WriteDiagnostic, LogControllerRayDiagnostics, DescribeHandSubsystems, and several internal helpers are called by HandTracking, ControllerRays, and the main controller file. TryGetTransformPropertyValue, TryGetObjectPropertyValue, and CachedHandSubsystems appear to be used only within Diagnostics itself.

Stripping Diagnostics.cs would break compilation. LogHands, LogHandsWarning, WriteDiagnostic, and LogControllerRayDiagnostics are called by production code. HandTracking uses GetRelativeTransformPath instead of GetHierarchyPath. Any removal of Diagnostics must preserve or replace those logging methods.

Diagnostics.cs mixes three distinct concerns. It contains true debug-only ray snapshot logging. It holds shared production logging infrastructure such as LogHands and WriteDiagnostic. It also includes DescribeHandSubsystems, which HandTracking needs at runtime. Because of this, the file cannot be safely removed without moving LogHands and DescribeHandSubsystems to another location first.

QuestXRInteractionController.Diagnostics.cs is not needed for gameplay. Its Update method runs every frame and always calls RefreshTrackedInteractionState. That method fetches four tracking statuses, possibly triggers reflection-based mode updates, queries input mode via reflection, and then performs a full native XR device scan inside SyncTrackedInteractionVisibility when piano mode is active. Each scan clears the cached device list, queries all XR devices, and iterates the results. If ray diagnostics are enabled, the controller then logs the results. enableControllerRayDiagnostics defaults to true, so this entire diagnostic path executes every single frame.

FindChildTransform allocates memory via GetComponentsInChildren<Transform>(true). ConfigureControllerRayOrigins runs both during tracking changes and inside ApplyInteractionMode. AndroidJNI logcat fires on every LogHands call, even during non-diagnostic support checks. SceneLoader and CambiadorEscenas appear to be duplicate classes.

More unused code identified. MIDIStatusReceiver.CurrentDeviceName, IsDiscoveryInProgress, and HasConfiguredServer appear unused. SongItem.SongMode and IsPianoMode are referenced. HistoryManager.navegacion is unused. SmoothFollowCanvas.enableFollowing is false. FindLoadedObjectOfType is used by HandTracking. CachedXRInputDevices is queried every frame.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Beginning to examine the Core scripts and related files.

Several unused fields and methods were identified across the Core scripts. MIDIStatusReceiver exposes CurrentDeviceName without external references. SongItem defines SongMode and IsPianoMode that appear unused elsewhere. HistoryManager carries a public navegacion field likely wired in the inspector but never read. DiscoverServerAsync and IsDiscoveryInProgress are unreachable from outside their classes. SceneLoader and CambiadorEscenas are duplicate wrapper classes. UDPReceiver.messageQueue is enqueued but never consumed, indicating dead legacy MIDI-over-UDP logic. PianoGame.unity scene contains both UDPBeacon and UDPReceiver components.

LoginScene also contains UDPBeacon and MIDIConnectionManager. Login.cs and Register.cs still attempt to resolve the MIDI device name even though MidiInitializer disables MIDI for those scenes. This creates a contradiction where the initializer blocks MIDI while the login and register flows continue to request it.

QuestXRInteractionController.Update runs RefreshTrackedInteractionState every frame. This triggers four XRInputTrackingAggregator status queries plus reflection-based input mode lookups. The piano scene additionally calls IsExactPhysicalControllerTracked twice per frame, which internally invokes InputDevices.GetDevices. Other scenes avoid this by reusing pre-fetched tracking data.

LogControllerRayDiagnostics allocates memory every time it runs. It queries all child transforms via GetComponentsInChildren<Transform>(true). It then fetches every MonoBehaviour under each transform through GetComponentsInChildren<MonoBehaviour>(true>. Reflection scans RayTransformFieldNames on each component. DescribeTransform reads world positions. These values change every frame. This makes the diagnostic log expensive to run.

The snapshot comparison inside the diagnostics is broken. DescribeTransform embeds position and rotation with three decimal places, so the pose data changes every frame. This means the “only log when changed” guard never skips execution, and the periodic 120-frame diagnostic fires continuously. Each diagnostic call also performs an AndroidJNI Log.i on the Quest device, adding JNI overhead.

LogHands emits verbose output during Awake, OnEnable, Start, and ApplyInteractionMode. FindChildTransform allocates a fresh Transform array on every call; it is invoked from ConfigureControllerRayOrigins and the diagnostics path. Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll appears in ConfigureUiInputModules and FindLoadedObjectOfType. EnvLoader blocks the main thread with a busy-wait loop while the startup operation completes. UDPReceiver spawns its own background thread inside Start.

UDPReceiver logs errors from its background thread. This is unsafe in Unity. The class has no OnDestroy. A scene unload leaves the thread running. UdpClient may throw. OnApplicationQuit waits up to five seconds to join the thread. This can stall shutdown. UDPBeacon broadcasts every three seconds forever. It logs a debug message each cycle. OnDisable closes the client socket. But the BroadcastPresence coroutine keeps running until the MonoBehaviour is destroyed. Every three seconds the code sends after close. This causes repeated errors. Both LoginScene and PianoGame contain UDPBeacon.

NetworkConfig UDP discovery uses port 5555 instead of the 8888 port used by other discovery mechanisms. It starts an async fire-and-forget routine that may throw exceptions, and it performs UDP receive operations on the main thread via async patterns. BackendConnectionManager rotates its spinner and positions its canvas every frame, even when the connection panel is hidden. It also polls health every five seconds while connected.

MidiStatusWidgetController runs PositionCanvas every LateUpdate to keep the widget following the camera. Its Update method throttles dependency resolution to 0.5 seconds, yet it still refreshes the badge pulse every frame and calls RefreshView every 0.1 seconds. RefreshView assigns numerous UI text properties each cycle even when the values have not changed. DirectMidiReceiver sets checkInterval to 0.001 seconds, but Update executes at roughly 11–13 milliseconds per frame, so the receiver effectively polls every frame.

DirectMidiReceiver performs JNI calls on every poll. It queries GetStatic isConnected and CallStatic getConnectedDeviceName each cycle. DrainPendingEvents can dequeue up to max(256, maxEventsPerFrame) events per frame. The Start method forces maxEventsPerFrame to at least 256, overriding inspector settings. All ConcurrentQueue enqueue and dequeue operations run on the main thread. This makes the queue unnecessary overhead. The receiver also reconnects every 1.5 seconds by rescanning devices through JNI. MIDIConnectionManager.Update runs every frame.

MIDIConnectionManager.Update calls EnsureStatusReceiver and RefreshStateFromReceiver every frame. RefreshStateFromReceiver may trigger FindObjectOfType. HandleMidiStatusUpdate runs each frame even when the MIDI state is unchanged. MIDIStatusReceiver.Update runs every 0.5 seconds. It tries to attach to the receiver via FindObjectOfType. It emits a warning log every half second when the receiver is missing. This warning spam occurs in LoginScene, RegisterScene, and SingGame where MIDI is disabled.

MidiInitializer.SetRuntimeState still locates DirectMidiReceiver and sets validationActive to false. MIDIStatusReceiver remains attached because its parent MIDIConnectionManager is DontDestroyOnLoad. LoginScene contains MIDIConnectionManager, so the receiver exists even when MIDI is disabled. This explains why the half-second warning spam in LoginScene persists despite the initializer skipping MIDI setup.

MidiInitializer skips EnableRuntimeSystems for LoginScene and sets runtime state to false. LoginScene still contains a MIDIConnectionManager instance, so the receiver searches for DirectMidiReceiver every 0.5 seconds and logs warnings. The initializer also creates a duplicate MIDIConnectionManager when entering piano scenes, even though LoginScene already owns one.

HarmonyEngineTests lives outside the Editor folder, so it compiles into the main assembly and executes on Quest after every scene load. The yaEjecutado flag guards it to once per app session, but the test still runs in production builds.

MIDIStatusReceiver redundantly polls HandleMidiStatusChange every 0.5 seconds even when subscribed. Comments are noisy and mix Spanish. Remaining model files will be reviewed next.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Prefab serialization appears to omit certain fields.

Several new fields were omitted from the prefab serialization. Unity falls back to C# defaults. Controller ray diagnostics are enabled by default. Hand tracking is disabled in the piano game scene. These defaults may cause unnecessary overhead.

FindChildTransform scans the entire hierarchy on every call. It is used in both diagnostics and ConfigureControllerRayOrigin. This creates repeated traversal overhead.

DirectMidiReceiver hardcodes maxEventsPerFrame to 256 during Start. This overrides the inspector value of 32. MidiAudioManager then drains the remaining queue each frame.

A logic bug disables MIDI during login because LoginScene is listed in MidiDisabledScenes. This sends a null device name.

HarmonyEngineTests runs in player builds on Quest. It logs nine test results plus a summary to logcat. It lacks an assembly definition and sits outside an Editor folder. The user wants these tests removed.

The final report will evaluate whether Diagnostics.cs is required at runtime.

Diagnose.cs is required at compile time because production HandTracking and ControllerRays call its logging helpers. The periodic snapshot logs inside Update are unnecessary for gameplay and defeat change detection. The recommendation is to guard diagnostic snapshots behind #if UNITY_EDITOR or DEVELOPMENT_BUILD, keep a lightweight no-op LogHands, and disable controller ray diagnostics by default.
</details></think>

# Core audit: `Assets/Scripts/Core/`

43 C# files. Highest Quest 3 cost is **XR tracking + diagnostics every frame**, then **JNI MIDI polling stacked on three Update loops**, then **legacy UDP**.

---

## 1. File list with purpose

### Midi/
| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `DirectMidiReceiver.cs` | Real MIDI path. JNI to `MidiInputBridge`, polled in `Update`, fills `messageQueue` for `MidiAudioManager`. |
| `MIDIConnectionManager.cs` | DontDestroyOnLoad singleton. Mirrors connection state, syncs device name to API. |
| `MIDIStatusReceiver.cs` | Extra poller/subscriber between `DirectMidiReceiver` and `MIDIConnectionManager`. |
| `MidiInitializer.cs` | `RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod`: creates MIDI runtime in piano/home scenes; disables it in Login/Register/SingGame. |
| `MidiStatusWidgetController.cs` | Floating MIDI badge + reconnect gate used by piano gameplay. |
| `MidiStatusWidgetController.Ui.cs` | Builds that UI at runtime. |

### Networking/
| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `UDPReceiver.cs` | **Legacy.** Background thread listens on UDP 12345. Queue is never consumed. Still on `PianoGame`. |
| `UDPBeacon.cs` | **Legacy.** Broadcasts `"ETHERIA_VR_DISCOVERY"` every 3s on port 5555. On Login + PianoGame. |
| `BackendConnectionManager.cs` | Health overlay + `ReportRequestResult`. Auto-created before first scene. |
| `AuthService.cs` | Login/register/songs/history/config HTTP. |

### VR/
| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `QuestXRInteractionController.cs` | Main XR rig controller on `XR Origin (XR Rig).prefab`. `Update` every frame. |
| `...Diagnostics.cs` | Logging + ray snapshots + Android logcat JNI. **Compile dependency**, not a gameplay system. |
| `...HandTracking.cs` | Hands install, permissions, visualizer wiring. |
| `...ControllerRays.cs` | Direct ray origin, UI fallbacks off. |
| `...Reflection.cs` | Private XRI field access. **Needed at runtime.** |
| `SmoothFollowCanvas.cs` | Camera follow, **off by default**. |
| `ReticleToLineEnd.cs` | Places reticle on line renderer end. |

### Session / Config / UI / Models
- `Initializer.cs` — touches `NetworkConfig.Instance` at boot.
- `UserSession.cs` — login singleton.
- `EnvLoader.cs` — reads `StreamingAssets/.env` (busy-waits on Quest).
- `NetworkConfig.cs` — backend URL; optional UDP discovery on **8888** (separate from Beacon 5555).
- UI: login/register, repertorio, history, graphs, alerts, scene wrappers.
- DTOs: login/register/songs/config/errors.

---

## 2. Performance issues (Quest 3 impact)

### P0 — XR diagnostics + tracking every frame

`enableControllerRayDiagnostics` **defaults to true**. The prefab does not serialize that field, so the default sticks:

```36:37:c:\Users\vic-s\Desktop\etheriavr_metaquest3\Assets\Scripts\Core\VR\QuestXRInteractionController.cs
    [SerializeField] private bool enableControllerRayDiagnostics = true;
    [SerializeField] private int controllerRayDiagnosticIntervalFrames = 120;
```

```83:94:c:\Users\vic-s\Desktop\etheriavr_metaquest3\Assets\Scripts\Core\VR\QuestXRInteractionController.cs
    private void Update()
    {
        RefreshTrackedInteractionState();

        if (!enableControllerRayDiagnostics) return;

        controllerRayDiagnosticFrameCounter++;
        if (controllerRayDiagnosticFrameCounter < Mathf.Max(1, controllerRayDiagnosticIntervalFrames)) return;

        controllerRayDiagnosticFrameCounter = 0;
        LogControllerRayDiagnostics("periodic", false);
    }
```

Every frame, `RefreshTrackedInteractionState()` queries four XR tracking statuses, reads private modality fields via reflection, and in PianoGame calls `InputDevices.GetDevices` **twice**:

```237:243:c:\Users\vic-s\Desktop\etheriavr_metaquest3\Assets\Scripts\Core\VR\QuestXRInteractionController.cs
        if (IsControllerOnlyModeEnabledForActiveScene())
        {
            leftShouldShowHand = false;
            rightShouldShowHand = false;
            leftShouldShowController = IsExactPhysicalControllerTracked(InputDeviceCharacteristics.Left);
            rightShouldShowController = IsExactPhysicalControllerTracked(InputDeviceCharacteristics.Right);
```

```291:294:c:\Users\vic-s\Desktop\etheriavr_metaquest3\Assets\Scripts\Core\VR\QuestXRInteractionController.cs
    private static bool TryGetDeviceWithExactCharacteristics(...)
    {
        CachedXRInputDevices.Clear();
        InputDevices.GetDevices(CachedXRInputDevices);
```

Periodic diagnostics walk the whole controller hierarchy (`GetComponentsInChildren<Transform>` and `MonoBehaviour`), then dump poses into a `StringBuilder`. Pose is in the snapshot, so “only log when changed” almost never skips:

```133:139:c:\Users\vic-s\Desktop\etheriavr_metaquest3\Assets\Scripts\Core\VR\QuestXRInteractionController.Diagnostics.cs
    private static string DescribeTransform(Transform transform)
    {
        if (transform == null) return "<null>";

        Vector3 position = transform.position;
        Vector3 rotation = transform.rotation.eulerAngles;
        return $"{GetHierarchyPath(transform)}@p({position.x:F3},{position.y:F3},{position.z:F3}) r(...)";
```

Every log also does **AndroidJNI `Log.i`** on device:

```180:194:c:\Users\vic-s\Desktop\etheriavr_metaquest3\Assets\Scripts\Core\VR\QuestXRInteractionController.Diagnostics.cs
    private void WriteDiagnostic(string message, bool isWarning)
    {
        string formattedMessage = $"[{DiagnosticTag}] {message}";
        if (isWarning) Debug.LogWarning(formattedMessage, this);
        else Debug.Log(formattedMessage, this);

#if UNITY_ANDROID && !UNITY_EDITOR
        using (AndroidJavaClass logClass = new AndroidJavaClass("android.util.Log"))
        {
            logClass.CallStatic<int>(isWarning ? "w" : "i", DiagnosticTag, message);
        }
```

`LogHands` is **unconditional** — `logConfigurationOnce` only gates one line. Awake/OnEnable/Start/hand install spam logcat.

`FindChildTransform` allocates a full `Transform[]` on every lookup.

### P0 — MIDI: JNI every frame + three overlapping Update loops

Then two more Update consumers:

On Login/Register/SingGame, MIDI is disabled, but `MIDIStatusReceiver` still searches and can warn **every 0.5s**:

### P1 — Legacy UDP still live in scenes

`UDPReceiver` starts a thread, binds port 12345, enqueues forever. **Nothing reads `messageQueue`.** Piano MIDI goes through JNI + `DirectMidiReceiver`. Present on `PianoGame.unity`.

`UDPBeacon` logs and broadcasts every 3s on Login + PianoGame. Different protocol from `NetworkConfig` discovery (port **8888**, `"ETHERIA_SEARCH"`).

`EnvLoader.ReadRawContent` busy-waits UnityWebRequest on the **main thread** on Android:

## 4. Duplicate MIDI status systems

Four layers do the same job:

1. **Source of truth:** `DirectMidiReceiver.OnConnectionStatusChanged` (JNI).
2. **`MIDIStatusReceiver`** — subscribes **and** re-polls every 0.5s.
3. **`MIDIConnectionManager.Update`** — re-reads receiver **every frame**, then fires the same event again.
4. **`MidiStatusWidgetController`** — FindObjectOfType + 0.1s UI refresh + its own event subscription.

Connection logs fire twice on one plug/unplug:

```184:184:c:\Users\vic-s\Desktop\etheriavr_metaquest3\Assets\Scripts\Core\Midi\DirectMidiReceiver.cs
        Debug.Log($"[MIDI] {(connected ? "CONECTADO" : "DESCONECTADO")}");
```

```33:33:c:\Users\vic-s\Desktop\etheriavr_metaquest3\Assets\Scripts\Core\Midi\MIDIStatusReceiver.cs
        Debug.Log($"... 🔔 ESTADO CAMBIÓ: {(isConnected ? "CONECTADO ✅" : "DESCONECTADO ❌")}");
```

```58:58:c:\Users\vic-s\Desktop\etheriavr_metaquest3\Assets\Scripts\Core\Midi\MIDIConnectionManager.cs
            Debug.Log($"... Estado MIDI: {(isConnected ? "CONECTADO" : "DESCONECTADO")}");
```

**Keep:** `DirectMidiReceiver` + widget (event-driven). **Fold or delete:** `MIDIStatusReceiver` and per-frame `MIDIConnectionManager.Update`.

Also two UDP discovery stacks: Beacon 5555 vs `NetworkConfig` 8888.

## 5. Logs, comments, emojis

**Emojis in player logs**
- MIDI status: 🔔 ✅ ❌ ⏳
- UDPReceiver: 🎹
- Graphs UI: ▼ (fine, not a log)

**Hot logs (every frame / every few seconds)**
- `[XRHandsDebug]` + logcat JNI
- UDPBeacon `"Gritando presencia en la red..."` every 3s
- MIDI status warning every 0.5s when receiver missing
- DirectMidiReceiver `verboseMidiLogging` (off by default)

**Colored Debug.Log** (`<color=green>`) — editor-only cosmetics; still string-allocates on device.

**Comments:** mostly useful Spanish XML docs. Noise: `CambiadorEscenas` “Obligatorio para cambiar escenas”; `SmoothFollowCanvas` ALL-CAPS “DESACTIVADO”. No TODO/FIXME in Core.

---

## 6. Threading issues

| Location | Issue |
|---|---|
| `UDPReceiver` | Dedicated thread + `UdpClient`. `Debug.LogError` from the **background thread**. No `OnDestroy` — scene unload leaves the thread/socket. `Join(5000)` on quit can hitch. Queue unbounded. |
| `DirectMidiReceiver.messageQueue` | `ConcurrentQueue` but enqueue **and** dequeue are main-thread (`Update` + `MidiAudioManager.Update`). Extra atomics for no cross-thread need. |
| `NetworkConfig.EnsureReadyInternalAsync` | `async Task` + `UdpClient` from ScriptableObject init (`_ = EnsureReadyAsync()` fire-and-forget). Off unless `ENABLE_UDP_DISCOVERY`. |
| `EnvLoader` | Main-thread spin-wait, not a worker thread. |
| `BackendConnectionManager` | Correct: waits on the Task from a coroutine. |

Auth HTTP is coroutine/`UnityWebRequest` — fine.

---

## 7. Is `QuestXRInteractionController.Diagnostics.cs` needed at runtime?

**The file is required to compile. The diagnostic snapshots are not required to play.**

Must stay (or move) because production code calls them:
- `LogHands` / `LogHandsWarning` — HandTracking, ControllerRays, Awake/Start
- `DescribeHandSubsystems()` — HandTracking
- `LogControllerRayDiagnostics(...)` — Update, resume, modality change, ray config

Safe to drop from **player** builds:
- Periodic `Update` snapshots
- Pose strings / `AppendRelevantComponentFields` reflection dump
- AndroidJNI logcat duplicate
- Default `enableControllerRayDiagnostics = true`

Reflection.cs **is** needed at runtime (XRI private fields). Diagnostics.cs is a debug dump bolted onto real logging.

---

## 8. HarmonyEngineTests — user wants them removed

`c:\Users\vic-s\Desktop\etheriavr_metaquest3\Assets\Tests\EditMode\HarmonyEngineTests.cs`

- **No `.asmdef`.** Not in an `Editor` folder. Compiles into **Assembly-CSharp**.
- `[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(AfterSceneLoad)]` runs **on Quest** after the first scene.
- `yaEjecutado` limits it to once per session, but it still logs 9 PASS/FAIL lines + a summary.
- Only consumer of this file; `HarmonyEngine` itself is used by `GameplayScoring.Evaluation.cs`.

Safe to delete `HarmonyEngineTests.cs` (+ `.meta`). Production scoring is unaffected.

---

## Refactor recommendations (Quest 3 impact)

1. **Kill XR diagnostics in player** — `enableControllerRayDiagnostics = false`; wrap `WriteDiagnostic` / periodic snapshots in `#if UNITY_EDITOR \|\| DEVELOPMENT_BUILD`; stop AndroidJNI `Log`. Biggest frame-time + logcat win.

2. **Stop per-frame XR device enumeration** — cache `InputDevices.GetDevices` or subscribe to `InputDevices.deviceConnected/Disconnected`; only refresh modality on change, not every `Update`.

3. **Collapse MIDI status to events** — delete `MIDIStatusReceiver`; remove `MIDIConnectionManager.Update`; keep JNI poll in `DirectMidiReceiver` only. Raise `checkInterval` to ~8–16 ms. Stop forcing `maxEventsPerFrame` to 256.

4. **Remove legacy UDP from PianoGame/Login** — delete or disable `UDPReceiver` + `UDPBeacon` components. Stops a wasted thread, bind, and 3s log spam.

5. **Gate overlay `LateUpdate`/`PositionCanvas`** — MIDI widget and backend overlay should follow the HMD only while visible.

6. **Strip player logs** — no emojis, no color tags, no per-frame `[XRHandsDebug]`. Keep errors/warnings.

7. **Delete `HarmonyEngineTests.cs`** from the player build.

8. **`EnvLoader`** — yield instead of `while (!operation.isDone)` to avoid a boot hitch.

9. **Cleanup (low FPS impact)** — merge `SceneLoader`/`CambiadorEscenas`; drop unused DTO/methods; make `MIDIConnectionManager` subscribe once instead of `FindObjectOfType` fallbacks.

10. **Keep** `QuestXRInteractionController.Reflection.cs` and the actual ray/hand config. That is the real XR product code.
